lead: Microsoft's Azure security cert, exam SC-500. It proves you can lock down identity, data, networks and compute in Azure and hybrid clouds, secure AI apps and agents, and run security posture and monitoring with Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel. It replaced Azure Security Engineer (AZ-500), which retired on Aug 31, 2026.
objSub: Four skill areas and 12 objectives from Microsoft's SC-500 study guide. Tick them off as you study; progress saves on this device.

cur.note: Replaced AZ-500, which retired Aug 31, 2026; AZ-500 can't be taken or renewed anymore, and it wasn't converted. Microsoft's certification page still showed SC-500 as beta when we checked, while training providers say it went live Jul 21, 2026. Check the page before you book.
cur.onote: Official Microsoft skill areas and objectives, in plain words. Microsoft gives weight ranges (20–25%, 25–30%, 20–25%, 20–25%); the bars use the middle of each range.

domains.name: Manage identity, access, and governance
obj: Secure access with Microsoft Entra ID
Privileged Identity Management (PIM), Conditional Access, MFA and passwordless, app registrations and enterprise apps, OAuth consent settings, and managed identities.
Secure secrets and keys with Azure Key Vault
Deploy and configure Key Vault, its access and firewall settings, keys, secrets and certificates; scan for exposed secrets with Defender CSPM; turn on Defender for Key Vault.
Governance for security and compliance

Azure Policy (built-in and custom), regulatory compliance in Defender for Cloud, resource locks, built-in and custom roles, fixing over-privileged access, secure backups, and security controls in infrastructure as code.

domains.name: Secure storage, databases, and networking
obj: Storage accounts
Storage account security settings, storage firewall rules, Defender for Storage, and access policies.
Databases
Platform security for Azure SQL, auditing for Azure SQL Database and Managed Instance, and Defender for Databases.
Network services

NSGs and application security groups, Azure Virtual Network Manager policies, Virtual WAN and VPN security, Entra Private Access, private endpoints and Private Link, Azure Firewall, and checking effective rules with Network Watcher.

domains.name: Secure compute
obj: Security for AI

Find oversharing in SharePoint, AI data risks with Purview DSPM, real-time protection for Copilot Studio agents, Entra Agent ID (Conditional Access, risk and access), an AI gateway in API Management for Microsoft Foundry, Defender for AI Services, agent guardrails in Foundry, and the Data and AI security dashboard.
Servers and virtual machines

Disk encryption, Azure Bastion, just-in-time (JIT) VM access, Azure Arc for hybrid and multicloud servers, Defender for Servers (vulnerability scanning and EDR), agentless scanning, secure boot and vTPM, and machine configuration.
Application platforms
Defender for Containers, AKS, Container Registry, Container Instances and Container Apps, Azure Functions, Logic Apps, App Service, Web Application Firewall, and API Management back-end protection.

domains.name: Manage and monitor security posture
obj: Posture with Defender for Cloud

Find risks with Defender CSPM, check compliance against frameworks, turn on workload protection plans, connect AWS and Google Cloud, configure Defender Vulnerability Management, and find exposed assets with Defender EASM.
Event collection in Microsoft Sentinel

Workspaces and roles, content hub solutions, data connectors for Azure, syslog and CEF collection, Windows security events with data collection rules, custom log tables, automation rules and playbooks, data retention, and Purview Audit in Defender XDR.
Microsoft Security Copilot
Workspaces, permissions and roles, plugins, and Microsoft and Security Store agents.

extras.title: Microsoft security tools
rows: Secure score, recommendations, compliance and workload protection plans
Which exposed resources can reach sensitive data, including AI
EDR, vulnerability scanning and JIT access
Image scanning and runtime threat detection
Threats like prompt injection against AI models
Sensitive data showing up in Copilot and AI app use
Collect logs, detect, investigate and automate the response
AI help for analysts, with plugins and agents

extras.title: Access, done right
rows: Admin roles only when needed, with approval and MFA
Allow, block or require MFA by user, device, place, risk
An Azure identity for an app; nothing to store or rotate
Keys, secrets and certs behind RBAC and a firewall
An identity for each AI agent, with its own access rules

extras.title: Lock down a VM
rows: No public IP. Admins connect through Azure Bastion.
Turn on just-in-time access so RDP and SSH open only on approved request.
Use a Trusted launch VM: secure boot and vTPM on.
Onboard it to Defender for Servers for EDR and vulnerability scanning.
Enforce settings with machine configuration and Azure Policy.

extras.title: How an NSG decides
rows: Inbound traffic must pass the subnet NSG, then the NIC NSG.
Rules run lowest priority number first; the first match wins.
Default rules (65000+): allow traffic inside the VNet, allow the Azure load balancer, deny everything else inbound.
Outbound to the internet is allowed by default. Add rules or Azure Firewall to limit it.

method: Use the four skill areas above. Storage, databases and networking is the biggest at 25–30%.
Read the SC-500 study guide line by line, then the Microsoft Learn docs for each tool. Use AZ-500 material only for the parts that didn't change.
In a personal Azure account: Key Vault with a managed identity, an NSG with ASGs, a private endpoint, Bastion with JIT, Defender for Cloud and a Sentinel workspace with one connector.
Flashcards for the security tools table, Entra access features, NSG rule order and what each Defender plan protects.
Try the exam sandbox, then timed practice questions labeled SC-500. Microsoft's own practice assessment wasn't out yet when we checked.
tips: About a quarter of the compute area is AI: Copilot Studio agents, Entra Agent ID, Foundry and Defender for AI. Most older courses skip it.
If the question says “prevent” or “ensure,” look for Azure Policy (Deny), Conditional Access or a lock. Defender and Sentinel find problems after they happen.
The best answer usually gives the narrowest role, for the shortest time (PIM), with no stored secret (managed identity).
Associate exams let you open Microsoft Learn during the test. Use it to confirm a setting, not to learn a topic.

items: The official skills list. Study straight from it.
Cloud and AI Security Engineer certification page
Posture, CSPM, workload plans and multicloud connectors.
Connectors, analytics, automation rules and playbooks.
Try case studies and the other question types.
Use a personal account and card, never a government card or work data. Defender plans and Sentinel cost money after their trials, so set a budget alert and clean up.
Make sure it says SC-500, not AZ-500. Much of the AI content is new.
Check the course was updated for SC-500 in 2026.

quiz.q: Admins should hold Global Administrator only when they need it, for a few hours, after approval and MFA. What should you use?
o: Privileged Identity Management with eligible assignments
Right. PIM makes admins eligible, and they activate the role just in time with approval and MFA.
Permanent role assignments plus a Conditional Access policy
Conditional Access protects sign-in, but the admin rights are still always on.
A custom role with fewer permissions
Fewer permissions is good, but it's still standing access, not time-limited.
A break-glass account for every admin
Break-glass accounts are for emergencies, and only one or two should exist.

quiz.q: A function app must read secrets from Key Vault without storing any credential in its settings. What's the BEST approach?
o: Give the function app a managed identity and the Key Vault Secrets User role on the vault
Right. Azure manages the identity's credentials, and the role grants read access to secrets only.
Put a client secret for an app registration in the app settings
That's a stored credential that can leak and must be rotated.
Use the storage account key
Unrelated to Key Vault, and it's a secret too.
Make the Key Vault public with no firewall
Public access doesn't give the app permission, and it weakens the vault.

quiz.q: No one may create a storage account that allows public blob access. Which control stops it at creation time?
o: An Azure Policy with the Deny effect
Right. Deny blocks the create or update request if it breaks the rule.
An Azure Policy with the Audit effect
Audit only flags it after it's created.
A Defender for Cloud recommendation
Recommendations tell you about the problem. They don't block it.
A resource lock on the subscription
Locks stop deletes and changes, not risky settings on new resources.

quiz.q: Web VMs may talk to database VMs only on TCP 1433. VMs are added to both tiers often. How do you write the NSG rule with the least upkeep?
o: Use application security groups: source ASG web, destination ASG db, port 1433
Right. New VMs just join the right ASG; the rule never changes.
List every VM's IP address in the rule
You'd edit the rule every time a VM is added or replaced.
Use only Azure Firewall for traffic inside the subnet
Overkill for VM-to-VM rules, and traffic inside a subnet doesn't go through it by default.
Turn off the NSGs and rely on the database's login
That removes the network control entirely.

quiz.q: A storage account must be reachable only from inside the unit's VNet, with public network access turned off. What do you configure?
o: A private endpoint, and set public network access to Disabled
Right. The account gets a private IP in the VNet, and the public endpoint stops answering.
A service endpoint
Traffic stays on Microsoft's network, but the account still uses its public endpoint.
A SAS token
A SAS controls what a caller can do, not which network it comes from.
A firewall rule that allows all networks
That's the opposite of what's needed.

quiz.q: Auditors want every login and query against Azure SQL Database recorded in a Log Analytics workspace. What do you turn on?
o: Auditing on the server or database, sending to Log Analytics
Right. SQL auditing records database events and can send them to a workspace.
Defender for SQL
Defender adds threat detection and vulnerability assessment. It isn't the audit log.
Transparent Data Encryption
TDE encrypts data at rest. It doesn't log activity.
Always Encrypted
It protects sensitive columns from the database's own admins. It doesn't log activity.

quiz.q: Outbound traffic from many VNets must be filtered centrally by domain name, with threat intelligence blocking known bad sites. What fits?
o: Azure Firewall in a hub VNet, with routes sending traffic through it
Right. Azure Firewall filters by FQDN and has threat intelligence.
NSGs on every subnet
NSGs filter by IP and port, not domain names, and aren't central.
Web Application Firewall
WAF protects inbound web traffic to your apps, not outbound browsing.
Azure Bastion
Bastion is for admin RDP and SSH.

quiz.q: RDP and SSH must be closed by default and open only on request, for a set time, from the requester's IP. What should you use?
o: Just-in-time VM access in Defender for Servers
Right. JIT opens the port briefly for an approved request, then closes it.
A permanent NSG rule allowing 3389 from the office
The port is open all the time.
Azure Bastion alone
Bastion avoids public IPs, but it doesn't open and close ports on request.
A VPN Gateway
A VPN reaches the network, but the ports stay open behind it.

quiz.q: Admins need RDP and SSH into VMs that have no public IP, without opening 3389 or 22 to the internet. What should you deploy?
o: Azure Bastion
Right. Bastion connects through the portal over TLS to VMs on private IPs.
A public IP on each VM with an NSG
That exposes every VM to the internet.
Microsoft Sentinel
Sentinel monitors. It doesn't provide access.
A jump box with a public IP
It works, but it's one more internet-facing server to patch and protect.

quiz.q: You need alerts when someone tries prompt injection or other attacks against your AI model deployments in Microsoft Foundry. What should you enable?
o: Defender for AI Services in Defender for Cloud
Right. It detects threats against AI workloads, like prompt injection and data leakage.
Defender for Storage
It protects storage accounts, not AI models.
Microsoft Purview DSPM
Purview tracks sensitive data in AI use. It isn't a threat detector for model attacks.
An NSG on the Foundry subnet
NSGs filter network traffic. A prompt is valid traffic.

quiz.q: Leadership wants to know which sensitive data people are pasting into Copilot and other AI apps. Which tool shows that?
o: Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) for AI
Right. It shows sensitive data in AI interactions and the risky activity around it.
Defender for AI Services
That watches for attacks on your AI deployments, not what users share.
Azure Monitor
Monitor shows performance and logs, not data sensitivity.
Conditional Access
It controls sign-in, not what users type.

quiz.q: You must scan images in Azure Container Registry for vulnerabilities and detect threats in running AKS clusters. Which plan?
o: Defender for Containers
Right. It covers registry scanning, AKS hardening checks and runtime threat detection.
Defender for Servers
It protects VMs and servers, not the container layer.
Azure Policy alone
Policy enforces settings. It doesn't scan images or detect attacks.
Defender EASM
EASM finds your internet-facing assets from the outside.

quiz.q: You need Linux syslog and firewall CEF logs flowing into Microsoft Sentinel. What do you set up?
o: The Azure Monitor Agent with a data collection rule, through Sentinel's syslog and CEF connectors
Right. The agent collects the logs, the data collection rule says what to send, and the connector brings them in.
Defender CSPM
CSPM is posture management. It doesn't collect syslog.
Microsoft Purview Audit
Purview Audit covers Microsoft 365 activity.
Defender EASM
EASM scans your external attack surface.

quiz.q: When a Sentinel incident shows a user account is compromised, the account should be disabled and the SOC channel notified automatically. What do you build?
o: An automation rule that runs a playbook (a Logic App)
Right. Automation rules trigger on incidents; playbooks take the actions.
An analytics rule only
Analytics rules create incidents. They don't take response actions.
A workbook
Workbooks are dashboards.
A watchlist
Watchlists hold reference data, like VIP users.

quiz.q: The unit also runs workloads in AWS and wants the same security recommendations and secure score for them. What should you do?
o: Connect the AWS accounts to Defender for Cloud
Right. Defender for Cloud has native AWS and Google Cloud connectors for posture and protection.
Only install Azure Arc on the AWS servers
Arc helps with servers, but the native connector covers the AWS account and its services.
Add the AWS connector to Sentinel only
That brings in AWS logs, not posture recommendations.
Use Defender EASM
EASM finds exposed assets. It doesn't assess AWS configuration.

pbqs.title: Pick the control
pbqs.scenario: Six requirements from the security plan. Pick the control that meets each one. Each answer is used once; four are distractors.

items.text: Admins get Global Administrator only for two hours, after approval.
items.why: PIM gives just-in-time, time-limited admin roles with approval.

items.text: Block sign-ins from outside the U.S. unless the device is compliant.
items.why: Conditional Access decides sign-ins by location, device and risk.

items.text: An app signs in to Azure services with no client secret or certificate to manage.
items.why: A managed identity's credentials are handled by Azure.

items.text: Nobody can create a storage account that allows public blob access.
items.why: A Deny policy blocks the create request.

items.text: Reach Azure SQL only over a private IP inside the VNet.
items.why: A private endpoint puts the service on a private IP in your VNet.

items.text: RDP to VMs that have no public IP, from the Azure portal.
items.why: Bastion connects to private VMs through the portal.

pbqs.title: Which tool shows it?
pbqs.scenario: Five questions from your commanding officer. Pick the Microsoft tool that answers each one. Each is used once; one is a distractor.

rows.req: Which internet-exposed VMs have a path to our sensitive data?
rows.why: Defender CSPM's attack path analysis shows exposed routes to sensitive resources.

rows.req: Which VMs have a critical vulnerability, and did EDR fire on any of them?
rows.why: Defender for Servers brings vulnerability scanning and EDR.

rows.req: Did anyone try a prompt injection against our Foundry model?
rows.why: Defender for AI Services alerts on attacks against AI workloads.

rows.req: Did anyone paste sensitive data into a Copilot chat?
rows.why: Purview DSPM for AI tracks sensitive data in AI interactions.

rows.req: Tie the firewall logs, sign-ins and alerts together into one incident.
rows.why: Sentinel correlates data from many sources into incidents.

pbqs.title: Allowed or denied?
pbqs.scenario: For each flow, decide what the NSGs do. Unless stated, only the default rules exist besides the ones listed.

rows.req: Inbound 3389 from the internet. Rules: priority 100 Deny 3389 from any; priority 200 Allow 3389 from Internet.
rows.why: Priority 100 is checked first and matches, so the traffic is denied.

rows.req: Inbound 443 from the internet. The only custom rule allows 443 from VirtualNetwork.
rows.why: The internet isn't VirtualNetwork, so the default DenyAllInbound blocks it.

rows.req: Outbound 443 to the internet. No custom outbound rules.
rows.why: The default AllowInternetOutBound rule allows it.

rows.req: Inbound 1433 from a web VM in the same VNet. The subnet NSG allows it; the NIC NSG has no custom rules.
rows.why: The NIC NSG's default AllowVnetInBound rule allows traffic between VNet addresses.

rows.req: Inbound health probe from the Azure load balancer. No custom rules.
rows.why: The default AllowAzureLoadBalancerInBound rule allows it.

mapSub: Cloud and AI Security Engineer is the top of the Microsoft cloud line. Tap any cert to jump to it.

keep.text: Microsoft role-based certs last one year. Renew for free by passing a short, open-book online assessment on Microsoft Learn.
keep.after: The assessment opens 6 months before your cert expires. Passing adds one year.

keep.text: AZ-500 and the Azure Security Engineer Associate cert retired on Aug 31, 2026. Holders can't renew it, and it wasn't converted to SC-500.
keep.after: If you hold AZ-500, keep listing it with its dates. SC-500 is the way to stay current.

keep.text: No Azure cert is on the DoD 8140 matrix (V3.0). For a coded billet, pair it with one that is, like CCSP or CISSP.
keep.after: Defense contractors often ask for both: an 8140 cert for the contract and a platform cert for the work.

keep.text: Check that CG COOL lists the new credential before you request funding. New certs can take time to appear.
keep.after: Renewals are free, so the exam fee is the only cost.
